guidelines.source: AAP Clinical Report — Fever and Antipyretic Use in Children (2011)
guidelines.notes: Standard weight-based dosing; caps at adult maximums.

guidelines.source: Manufacturer label — Children's Tylenol dosing chart, 2–3 years (24–35 lb)
guidelines.notes: Label: use weight if possible, otherwise age. Every 4 hours while symptoms last; not more than 5 times in 24 hours. Under 2 years (under 24 lb): ask a doctor.

guidelines.source: Manufacturer label — Children's Tylenol dosing chart, 4–5 years (36–47 lb)
guidelines.notes: Label: use weight if possible, otherwise age. Every 4 hours while symptoms last; not more than 5 times in 24 hours. Under 2 years (under 24 lb): ask a doctor.

guidelines.source: Manufacturer label — Children's Tylenol dosing chart, 6–8 years (48–59 lb)
guidelines.notes: Label: use weight if possible, otherwise age. Every 4 hours while symptoms last; not more than 5 times in 24 hours. Under 2 years (under 24 lb): ask a doctor.

guidelines.source: Manufacturer label — Children's Tylenol dosing chart, 9–10 years (60–71 lb)
guidelines.notes: Label: use weight if possible, otherwise age. Every 4 hours while symptoms last; not more than 5 times in 24 hours. Under 2 years (under 24 lb): ask a doctor.

medications.description: NSAID with antipyretic and analgesic effects.

guidelines.source: AAP Clinical Report — Fever and Antipyretic Use in Children (2011)
guidelines.notes: Not recommended under 6 months of age.

guidelines.source: Manufacturer label — Children's Motrin dosing chart

embodiments.label: 4% vaginal cream (25 g tube)
embodiments.notes: Miconazole nitrate vaginal cream USP 4%. 3-day treatment: one applicatorful at bedtime for 3 nights. (up&up Miconazole 3, NDC 11673-391-06)

embodiments.label: 1% cream (28.4 g tube)
embodiments.notes: Topical antifungal. Apply a thin layer twice daily. (CVS Health, NDC 59779-305-02)

medications.name: Diphenhydramine
medications.description: Antihistamine for allergy symptoms; causes drowsiness.

embodiments.label: 12.5 mg/5 mL oral solution (Children's)
embodiments.notes: Children 2 to 5 years: do not use unless directed by a doctor. Children under 2 years: do not use. Do not use with any other product containing diphenhydramine, even one used on the skin. Do not use to make a child sleepy; marked drowsiness may occur.

guidelines.source: Manufacturer label — Children's Allergy Relief (diphenhydramine) dosing chart, 6–11 years
guidelines.notes: Label: 5 mL to 10 mL (12.5–25 mg) every 4 to 6 hours, or as directed by a doctor; not more than 6 doses in 24 hours. The dose here is the top of that range; smaller doses are not flagged.

embodiments.label: 10 mg chewable tablet (Children's)
embodiments.notes: Chew thoroughly before swallowing. Children under 6 years: do not use. If you do not know whether a prescription drug contains an MAOI, ask a doctor or pharmacist before taking. Stop use and ask a doctor if cough lasts more than 7 days, comes back, or occurs with fever, rash or headache.

guidelines.source: Manufacturer label — Mucinex Children's Mighty Chews Cough, 6 to under 12 years
guidelines.notes: Label: 1 chewable tablet every 4 hours or as directed by a doctor; not more than 6 chewable tablets in any 24-hour period.

guidelines.source: Manufacturer label — Mucinex Children's Mighty Chews Cough, 12 years and over
guidelines.notes: Label: adults and children 12 years and over, 2 chewable tablets every 4 hours or as directed by a doctor; not more than 12 chewable tablets in any 24-hour period. No upper age on the label; 1500 months is the highest the guideline model accepts.
